title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 29 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 29.

questions.question: Who did David say God had chosen to build the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon his son
questions.explanation: David stated that Solomon his son, whom alone God hath chosen, is to build the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 29:1).

questions.question: What materials did David say he had prepared for the house of God?
options: Gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and precious stones
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and precious stones
questions.explanation: David prepared gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, onyx stones, glistering stones, and many precious stones (1 Chronicles 29:2).

questions.question: How much gold did David say he had given of his own proper good for the house of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Three thousand talents of gold
questions.explanation: David gave three thousand talents of gold of the gold of Ophir for the house of God (1 Chronicles 29:4).

questions.question: Who offered willingly to consecrate their service unto the LORD?
options: Chief of the fathers, princes, captains of thousands and hundreds, and rulers of the king's work
questions.correctAnswer: Chief of the fathers, princes, captains of thousands and hundreds, and rulers of the king's work
questions.explanation: These leaders offered willingly to consecrate their service unto the LORD (1 Chronicles 29:6).

questions.question: What was the amount of iron given for the service of the house of God?
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred thousand talents
questions.explanation: They gave one hundred thousand talents of iron for the service of the house of God (1 Chronicles 29:7).

questions.question: Who was given the precious stones to treasure for the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehiel the Gershonite
questions.explanation: Precious stones were given to Jehiel the Gershonite to be put in the treasure of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 29:8).

questions.question: True or False: The people rejoiced because they offered willingly and with a perfect heart to the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The people rejoiced because they offered willingly with perfect heart, and David also rejoiced with great joy (1 Chronicles 29:9).

questions.question: What did David say belongs to the LORD, including greatness, power, and glory?
options: All that is in heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: All that is in heaven and earth
questions.explanation: David declared that all that is in heaven and in the earth belongs to the LORD, including greatness, power, and glory (1 Chronicles 29:11).

questions.question: True or False: David said that riches and honour come from men.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David said riches and honour come from the LORD, who reigns over all (1 Chronicles 29:12).

questions.question: According to David, what is the nature of our days on the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: As a shadow
questions.explanation: David said our days on earth are as a shadow, and there is none abiding (1 Chronicles 29:15).

questions.question: Who, according to 1 Chronicles 29, is to be given a perfect heart to keep God's commandments?
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon
questions.explanation: David prayed that Solomon his son would be given a perfect heart to keep God's commandments (1 Chronicles 29:19).

questions.question: What did the congregation do after David said, 'Now bless the LORD your God'?
options: They blessed the LORD God, bowed their heads, and worshipped
They offered sacrifices to other gods
questions.correctAnswer: They blessed the LORD God, bowed their heads, and worshipped
questions.explanation: The congregation blessed the LORD God, bowed their heads, and worshipped the LORD and the king (1 Chronicles 29:20).

questions.question: True or False: On the day after the congregation blessed the LORD, they sacrificed a thousand bullocks, rams, and lambs with drink offerings.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: They sacrificed a thousand bullocks, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs with their drink offerings on the morrow after that day (1 Chronicles 29:21).

questions.question: Who was anointed chief governor when Solomon was made king?
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon
questions.explanation: Solomon was anointed unto the LORD to be the chief governor when he was made king (1 Chronicles 29:22).

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 29, which event came first?
options: David blessed the LORD before all the congregation
The princes submitted themselves to Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: David blessed the LORD before all the congregation
questions.explanation: David blessed the LORD before all the congregation first (verse 10), then later the people sacrificed offerings and Solomon was anointed (verses 21-22).

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 29:11, what attributes belong to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Greatness, power, glory, victory, majesty
questions.explanation: Verse 11 explicitly lists these attributes as belonging to the LORD: greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty. This is supported by the verse's declaration that all that is in heaven and earth is His and that He is exalted as head above all.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 29:12 describe the source of riches and honor?
options: They come from the LORD, who reigns over all
They come from human effort and wisdom
They come from the king's blessings
They come from the people's generosity
questions.correctAnswer: They come from the LORD, who reigns over all
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that both riches and honor come from God, who reigns over all, and that power and might are in His hand. This emphasizes divine sovereignty as the source of all blessings.

questions.question: What is the response of David and the people to God's greatness in 1 Chronicles 29:13?
options: They thank God and praise His glorious name
They offer sacrifices and burnt offerings
They build a house for God
questions.correctAnswer: They thank God and praise His glorious name
questions.explanation: Verse 13 shows the appropriate response to God's greatness is thanksgiving and praise of His glorious name, demonstrating faith and worship.

questions.question: What attitude does David express in 1 Chronicles 29:14 regarding their ability to offer generously to God?
options: Humility, recognizing all comes from God
Confidence in their wealth and power
questions.correctAnswer: Humility, recognizing all comes from God
questions.explanation: Verse 14 expresses humility, questioning who they are that they can offer so willingly, acknowledging that everything comes from God and they have only given what is His.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 29:15, how are the people described in relation to their time on earth?
options: Strangers and sojourners, with days as a shadow
Kings and conquerors, with eternal reign
Builders and workers, with lasting monuments
Priests and prophets, with divine calling
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers and sojourners, with days as a shadow
questions.explanation: Verse 15 describes the people as strangers and sojourners like their ancestors, emphasizing the temporary nature of life on earth, likened to a shadow.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 29:16, David acknowledges that all the resources prepared to build God's house come from where?
options: The hand of the LORD; they are all His own
The labor of the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The hand of the LORD; they are all His own
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clearly states that all the store prepared to build the house for God's holy name comes from the LORD's hand and belongs to Him, emphasizing God's ownership over all.

questions.question: What does David say about God’s examination of the heart and His pleasure in 1 Chronicles 29:17?
options: God tries the heart and has pleasure in uprightness
God values wealth and offerings above all
God judges only the actions, not the heart
questions.correctAnswer: God tries the heart and has pleasure in uprightness
questions.explanation: Verse 17 teaches that God examines the heart's intent and delights in uprightness, highlighting the importance of sincerity in offerings and worship.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 29:18, what does David ask God to do for the people’s hearts?
options: Keep upright thoughts and prepare their hearts unto God
questions.correctAnswer: Keep upright thoughts and prepare their hearts unto God
questions.explanation: Verse 18 is a prayer asking God to preserve the uprightness of the people’s hearts and to prepare them to serve Him faithfully.

questions.question: What specific request does David make for Solomon in 1 Chronicles 29:19?
options: That Solomon’s heart be perfect to keep God's commandments and build the palace
That Solomon be granted power to conquer enemies
That Solomon receive wealth and long life
That Solomon be made priest over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: That Solomon’s heart be perfect to keep God's commandments and build the palace
questions.explanation: Verse 19 shows David’s prayer for Solomon to have a perfect heart to obey God's laws and successfully build the palace prepared for God’s name.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 29:20 describe the congregation’s response when David asks them to bless the LORD?
options: They blessed the LORD, bowed their heads, and worshipped the LORD and the king
They ignored the request and continued their work
They scattered to their homes without response
questions.correctAnswer: They blessed the LORD, bowed their heads, and worshipped the LORD and the king
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states that the congregation obediently blessed the LORD, bowed their heads, and worshipped both God and the king, showing reverence and unity.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Chronicles 29:14, David teaches that all things come from man’s own strength and ability.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 14 explicitly says all things come from God and what they give is from His own, rejecting the idea that offerings come from human strength or ability alone.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Chronicles 29:15 compares human life to a shadow, emphasizing its fleeting nature.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 15 uses the metaphor of a shadow to describe the transient nature of human life on earth, highlighting humility and dependence on God.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 29:17, David admits that God does not care about the heart but only about the offerings themselves.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 17 clearly states that God tries the heart and takes pleasure in uprightness, so He cares deeply about the sincerity behind the offerings, not just the offerings themselves.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 29:19 imply about the relationship between obedience to God's commandments and leadership?
options: A perfect heart to keep commandments is essential for Solomon to build the palace and lead well
Leadership depends primarily on military strength
Wealth determines the success of a leader
Popularity among the people is the key to successful leadership
questions.correctAnswer: A perfect heart to keep commandments is essential for Solomon to build the palace and lead well
questions.explanation: Verse 19 links Solomon’s leadership and building of the palace with his obedience to God's laws, highlighting faithfulness as foundational for godly leadership.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 29:13 and 29:18, how does praise and prayer affect the hearts of God's people?
options: Praise leads to thanksgiving, and prayer secures God’s help in preparing hearts for Him
Praise is only for the king, and prayer is for the priests
Praise and prayer are unrelated to the people's hearts
Praise replaces the need for prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Praise leads to thanksgiving, and prayer secures God’s help in preparing hearts for Him
questions.explanation: Verse 13 shows praise as a response of thanks, while verse 18 is a prayer asking God to keep upright thoughts and prepare hearts. Together they demonstrate active worship shaping the people's hearts.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 29.

questions.question: What was the quantity of bullocks, rams, and lambs sacrificed to the LORD after David's address?
questions.correctAnswer: One thousand of each
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 29:21 states that they sacrificed a thousand bullocks, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, along with drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

questions.question: Who was anointed as the chief governor at Solomon's second coronation?
questions.correctAnswer: Zadok
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 29:22, Zadok was anointed to be priest, and Solomon was anointed to be the chief governor.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people after Solomon was anointed king the second time?
options: They ate and drank with great gladness
questions.correctAnswer: They ate and drank with great gladness
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 29:22 tells us that the people ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great gladness following Solomon's second anointing.

questions.question: How long did David reign in Jerusalem according to 1 Chronicles 29?
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty-three years
questions.explanation: Verse 27 states David reigned for forty years in total, seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which three books contain the acts of David as mentioned in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel, Nathan, Gad
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 29:29 explicitly mentions the acts of David are recorded in the book of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer.

questions.question: Which phrase correctly describes David's death as recorded in this chapter?
options: He died young and in battle
He died in exile and sorrow
He died in a good old age full of days, riches, and honour
questions.correctAnswer: He died in a good old age full of days, riches, and honour
questions.explanation: Verse 28 describes David's death as occurring in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honour.

questions.question: What literary device is seen in David’s prayer of praise that emphasizes God’s sovereignty over heaven and earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 use parallelism extensively, repeating and balancing phrases about God's greatness, power, and reign over all creation, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: According to David's prayer, what is the source of all riches and honor?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 29:12 says, 'Both riches and honour come of thee,' indicating God as the source of all wealth and glory.

questions.question: What does David ask God to give Solomon in his prayer?
options: A perfect heart to keep God's commandments
questions.correctAnswer: A perfect heart to keep God's commandments
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 29:19 requests God to give Solomon a perfect heart to keep His commandments, testimonies, and statutes to build the palace.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 29, all the princes, mighty men, and sons of David submitted themselves to Solomon as king.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 24 clearly states that all the princes, mighty men, and sons of King David submitted themselves to Solomon the king.

questions.question: True or False: David’s reign over Israel lasted thirty years according to this chapter.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 29:27 states David reigned forty years, not thirty.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God testing the heart and delighting in uprightness as David prays in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 7:9
questions.explanation: Psalm 7:9 speaks about God trying the heart and righteous, which parallels David's prayer in 1 Chronicles 29:17 where God tests the heart and delights in uprightness.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'perfect' as used in the phrase 'a perfect heart' given to Solomon in 1 Chronicles 29:19 most closely means:
questions.correctAnswer: Complete or whole
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'tamim' translated as 'perfect' (1 Chronicles 29:19) means 'complete' or 'whole,' signifying integrity and wholeheartedness, not sinless perfection.

questions.question: How does the theme of David’s prepared provisions for the temple in this chapter fulfill earlier Scripture commands regarding the temple construction?
options: It contradicts the command to build by the Levites alone
It fulfills the prophetic instructions about temple materials and offerings
It ignores the instructions given to Moses
It introduces a new temple concept not found before
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the prophetic instructions about temple materials and offerings
questions.explanation: David’s preparation and offerings for the temple (verses 1-5) fulfill earlier prophetic and Mosaic instructions about the temple's holiness and materials, showing continuity with God's plan in Exodus and Deuteronomy.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the cultural and historical significance of David’s reign length as recorded here?
options: Typical reign length in ancient Near Eastern monarchies
Long reign indicating political stability and divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Long reign indicating political stability and divine favor
questions.explanation: David’s forty-year reign (verses 26-27) reflects a long and stable rule, which in the ancient Near East was often interpreted as a sign of divine favor and successful governance.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David emphasize about Solomon's role and the nature of the palace in 1 Chronicles 29:1?
options: Solomon is chosen by God and the palace is for the LORD God, not man
Solomon is the strongest warrior and the palace is a symbol of military power
Solomon should rule with human wisdom and the palace is a royal residence
Solomon is inexperienced and the palace is an ordinary building
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon is chosen by God and the palace is for the LORD God, not man
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 29:1 states that Solomon is the son chosen by God and that the palace is not for man but for the LORD God, highlighting divine election and the sacred purpose of the building.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 29:4, what materials did David give specifically to overlay the walls of the house?
options: Three thousand talents of gold and seven thousand talents of refined silver
Five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand talents of silver
Seven thousand talents of gold and three thousand talents of silver
Ten thousand talents of gold and five thousand talents of silver
questions.correctAnswer: Three thousand talents of gold and seven thousand talents of refined silver
questions.explanation: Verse 4 explicitly mentions David providing three thousand talents of gold from Ophir and seven thousand talents of refined silver to overlay the walls of the house, emphasizing the costly and sacred nature of the temple construction.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 29:9 reveal about the people's attitude toward giving for the house of God?
options: They gave willingly and with perfect heart, causing David to rejoice greatly
They gave reluctantly and under compulsion
They gave only a small portion out of necessity
They did not give and were reprimanded by David
questions.correctAnswer: They gave willingly and with perfect heart, causing David to rejoice greatly
questions.explanation: Verse 9 describes the people's willingness and perfect heart in offering to the LORD, which brought great joy to David, highlighting the doctrine of joyful and voluntary giving in worship.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 29:11, which attributes of God are highlighted in David's blessing before the congregation?
options: Greatness, power, glory, victory, majesty, and exalted headship
questions.correctAnswer: Greatness, power, glory, victory, majesty, and exalted headship
questions.explanation: David blesses God by acknowledging His greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty, and that He is exalted as head above all, emphasizing God’s sovereign and majestic rule (1 Chronicles 29:11).

questions.question: What theological doctrine is expressed in David's statement in 1 Chronicles 29:14 about giving to God?
options: All things come from God and giving back is from His own blessings
Giving is optional and not required of believers
Only the wealthy are obligated to give
God requires giving as a condition for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: All things come from God and giving back is from His own blessings
questions.explanation: Verse 14 teaches the doctrine of divine providence and stewardship: everything originates from God and what is given back is from what He has already provided, grounding giving in gratitude and recognition of God's ownership.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 29:15, how does David describe the human condition before God?
options: As strangers and sojourners with days on earth like a shadow
As kings and rulers over the earth
As eternal beings who do not die
As permanent owners of the land
questions.correctAnswer: As strangers and sojourners with days on earth like a shadow
questions.explanation: David acknowledges humanity’s transient nature, describing people as strangers and sojourners with life like a fleeting shadow, emphasizing the doctrine of human frailty and the temporality of earthly existence (1 Chronicles 29:15).

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated in 1 Chronicles 29:17 where David says God 'trieth the heart' and has pleasure in uprightness?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omniscience and holiness
questions.explanation: The verse reveals God's omniscience in testing hearts and His holiness in delighting in uprightness, showing the moral purity God requires and His intimate knowledge of human intentions.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 1 Chronicles 29:10-12 and 1 Chronicles 29:16 convey about God's sovereignty and providence?
options: God is sovereign over all creation, possessing power, riches, and honor, and all provision comes from His hand
God is distant and uninvolved in human affairs
God's power is limited to Israel only
Riches and honor come from human effort, not God
questions.correctAnswer: God is sovereign over all creation, possessing power, riches, and honor, and all provision comes from His hand
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 proclaim God's greatness, power, and rule over all, while verse 16 affirms that everything prepared for the temple comes from God's hand, illustrating God's comprehensive sovereignty and providential care.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 29:19 reveal the theological importance of Solomon's heart condition for his future leadership?
options: God prays for Solomon to have a perfect heart to keep His commandments and build the temple
Solomon’s leadership depends on his military skills
Solomon’s wealth will secure his reign
Solomon is expected to rule without regard to God’s law
questions.correctAnswer: God prays for Solomon to have a perfect heart to keep His commandments and build the temple
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes the necessity of a pure and obedient heart in leadership, showing that Solomon’s success depends on divine enablement to follow God's law and fulfill the temple-building task.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 29:23 teach about Solomon’s reign and Israel’s response to his kingship?
options: Solomon prospered and all Israel obeyed him as king
Solomon ruled poorly and Israel rebelled
Solomon was a weak king and had little support
Solomon shared the throne with his brothers
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon prospered and all Israel obeyed him as king
questions.explanation: This verse emphasizes Solomon's prosperous reign and the unity of Israel under his leadership, reflecting God's blessing and the people's acceptance of his divinely appointed kingship.

questions.question: What apologetic response does 1 Chronicles 29:14-16 provide against the sceptical claim that human generosity is merely self-serving or forced?
options: It shows giving is a willing act recognizing God’s sovereign ownership and our transient status
It teaches that giving is compulsory and enforced by law
It suggests giving is rewarded with earthly riches
It claims that giving is irrelevant to faith
questions.correctAnswer: It shows giving is a willing act recognizing God’s sovereign ownership and our transient status
questions.explanation: Verses 14-16 teach that giving flows from recognizing all comes from God and that humans are temporary stewards, countering sceptical views by affirming genuine, willing generosity rooted in faith and humility.

questions.question: How do 1 Chronicles 29:20-22 narrate the transition of leadership from David to Solomon within Israel’s covenant community?
options: The people bless God, worship, sacrifice abundantly, and anoint Solomon as king and chief governor
David dies suddenly without a formal succession
Solomon seizes power by force with no people's approval
The people reject Solomon and demand another leader
questions.correctAnswer: The people bless God, worship, sacrifice abundantly, and anoint Solomon as king and chief governor
questions.explanation: These verses describe a solemn, covenantal transition marked by worship, sacrifice, and anointing, portraying divine approval and communal acceptance of Solomon’s kingship.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 29:25 reveal about God's special favor towards Solomon compared to previous kings of Israel?
options: The LORD magnified Solomon exceedingly and bestowed unprecedented royal majesty
Solomon was treated like all other kings with no special distinction
Solomon was rejected by God because of his youth
Solomon received less favor than his predecessors
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD magnified Solomon exceedingly and bestowed unprecedented royal majesty
questions.explanation: Verse 25 explicitly states that God exalted Solomon above all previous kings with extraordinary majesty, highlighting divine election and blessing in Solomon’s reign.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human kingship and divine authority is conveyed by 1 Chronicles 29:26-27 regarding David’s reign?
options: David reigned over all Israel for 40 years by God’s appointment, showing divine sovereignty over kingship
David seized power unlawfully and reigned without God’s blessing
David’s reign was short and insignificant
David ruled only a small tribe, not all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: David reigned over all Israel for 40 years by God’s appointment, showing divine sovereignty over kingship
questions.explanation: These verses summarize David’s long, divinely authorized reign over all Israel, affirming the doctrine that earthly kingship is under God’s sovereign rule.

questions.question: What synthesis of 1 Chronicles 29:3-5 and 1 Chronicles 29:7 reveals about the communal nature of worship and dedication in David’s time?
options: David and the tribal leaders gave generously from their own resources, showing corporate willingness in sacred service
Only David gave materials, while the people contributed nothing
Worship was limited to verbal praise without material offerings
The people were forced to give under threat of punishment
questions.correctAnswer: David and the tribal leaders gave generously from their own resources, showing corporate willingness in sacred service
questions.explanation: Verses 3-5 and 7 detail the personal and collective giving of David and the tribal leaders, emphasizing voluntary, generous dedication by the whole community for God’s house.
